ubuntu_systemd_259_5.exact_candidate: Ubuntu 26.04 systemd 259.5-0ubuntu3.4; archive verification and actual binary/QEMU checks belong to the root task

upstream_baseline.meaning: Backported 4.19 stays below upstream supported version baseline even if selected APIs are supplied.

source_confirmed_requirements.behavior: pidref_set_pid only accepts resource exhaustion as fallback; ENOSYS is an error. Kernel9 does not implement pidfd_open, so this is a concrete integration blocker to investigate with exact Ubuntu binary boot.
systemd mounts cgroup2 with nsdelegate; kernel9 has cgroup2, but controller/delegation/sandbox behavior must be tested and existing ASUS ownership must be migrated.

must_not_misclassify_as_259_universal_bo.behavior: 259.5 tries file handles and /proc/self/fdinfo when the statx mount-root attribute is absent; unlike the tested262 branch.
259.5 retains unsupported/privilege-error fallback; unlike the262 branch.
259.5 probes this optional mount option before using it, rather than demanding it unconditionally.

historical_262_test.actual_failure: STATX_ATTR_MOUNT_ROOT absence made early API filesystem setup fail; exact262 test used custom BE98 glibc2.44 and minimal262 build
historical_262_test.boundary: This is not proof that Ubuntu259.5 fails at the same point. Do not reuse262 missing-API list as259 acceptance result.

ubuntu_systemd_259_5.kernel9_scope: time64 patch does not add pidfds/new mount API or modern cgroup features; native arm64 time_t64 was already present. Three-ABI timer tests establish their tested libc/kernel paths only.

hard_evidence.missing_in_reference: __snprintf@GLIBC_PRIVATE is absent (the distinct __snprintf_chk@GLIBC_2.4 is present); copying only new libc breaks this consumer dependency.

glibc_transition.be98_reusable_fix: systemd-rc-compat-20260916 rebuilt libxcrypt4.4.38 with obsolete ABI and verified all original export names/versions plus DES/MD5 vectors. Reuse recipe, then compare BE19000AI libcrypt exports and run actual relocations; do not blindly reuse the BE98 binary.
glibc_transition.package_rule: Coordinate new loader, libc6, libc-bin, libc6-dev and ABI companions through dpkg packages. No untracked overwrite of Ubuntu libc6 files. Maintain armel, armhf and arm64 runtime closures separately.
glibc_transition.legacy_structure_abi: Default all newly built components to time64 (ARM32 _TIME_BITS=64 plus _FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64; native arm64 naturally64). At observed vendor boundaries use fixed-width protocol structs/versioned APIs and checked conversion, as BE98 successfully did while preserving application time64. Retain a legacy time32 component only as documented fallback, never blanket armel flags.
other_closure_risks: rc imports about40 direct libraries, including old libjson-c.so.2 plus vendor libai/libcfgmnt/libshared/libnvram; SONAME, symbol versions, plugin dlopen paths and structure ABI must be checked recursively.

Do not merge different vendor/distribution libraries only because SONAME matches. Keep vendor-private dependencies in per-ABI vendor directories with explicit per-program linkage until replacement is proven.
Closed-source armel stays armel. Existing AArch64 vendor executables stay arm64. armhf is optional for separately added applications, not a migration of the current SDK.

filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.required_change: Under systemd, early filesystem ownership must belong to the new init path; rc must not remount over systemd-owned trees or invalidate runtime sockets.

filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.finding: sysinit truncates /etc/hosts and /etc/fstab, links /rom/etc entries into /etc, rewrites resolv.conf and invokes ldconfig
filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.required_change: Persistent Ubuntu /etc and package conffiles cannot use stock /etc -> tmp/etc lifecycle. Preserve only explicitly owned ASUS generated files and migrate them without erasing apt/fstab/machine-id configuration.

filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.finding: legacy creates /tmp/etc and /var/run,/var/lib,/var/cache paths during boot
filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.required_change: Use tmpfs /run, /var/run -> /run, durable /var/lib/dpkg and /var/lib/apt, and /var/cache/apt; no volatile /var overlay that loses package state.

filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.finding: ASUS reboot action directly signals PID1 (SIGTERM/SIGQUIT)
filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.required_change: Retarget only ASUS manager notification/reboot paths via a validated broker; do not redirect arbitrary kill() calls or fake getpid().

filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.finding: service entry points distinguish PID1 manager from ordinary callers
filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.required_change: Port BE98 explicit manager role checks and peer-validated notification broker to this board-specific rc; source-wide matches include inactive models and are not execution counts.

filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.finding: AI service has explicit ai_reboot/ai_upgrade action dispatch
filesystem_and_pid1_conflicts.required_change: Preserve AI bridge/control as explicit separate actions; ordinary Wi-Fi/HTTP/port operations must not invoke AI-board reboot or firmware actions.

be98_reuse.reuse: Collision-rejecting merge script, root-relative symlink resolver, original-path/mode/hash checks and dynamic loader closure tests. Candidate exact aliases matched inspected Ubuntu base-files. Rerun on AI files; prior collision policy hashes are board-specific.

Triplet migration with compatibility links and explicit libdir, plus ABI export comparisons. Its early blanket legacy time-bits flags are historical and must not be copied into the new time64-default policy. Use the later AiMesh shared-memory fix as the compatibility pattern.
Explicit rc manager PID, root peer credentials, fixed SOCK_SEQPACKET protocol, notify_rc shims per ABI, linker wraps, readiness, subreaper, ordered shutdown and fail-closed absence checks.
NVRAM/config/hardware order stays in rc while units own daemon lifetime. 23 low-level platform units were tested offline; inspect latest cumulative corrections, not this checkpoint alone.
Platform candidate explicitly requires subsequent httpd-dashboard-fix and aimesh-ui-fix checkpoints; stale platform candidate has known SIGABRT/client-table defects.

service_orchestration_policy.first_compatible_cutover: systemd PID1 -> native arm64 authenticated broker -> board-specific armel rc manager. Preserve hardware startup order initially, then transfer independently testable daemon groups.
service_orchestration_policy.ownership: Exactly one owner per daemon. rc creates ASUS config and requests explicit units; unit supervisor owns PID/cgroup/restart/stop. No failure fallback to a duplicate legacy launcher.
service_orchestration_policy.network: Keep Broadcom driver/Runner/bridge/VLAN/WAN/DHCP/firewall policy under audited ASUS path initially. Do not enable Ubuntu networkd, NetworkManager, dnsmasq or resolved to compete for the same interfaces/ports/DNS path.
service_orchestration_policy.targeted_restart: Wi-Fi setting dispatches the smallest supported ASUS radio/service action; web/collector changes restart only corresponding units. Ethernet port changes need hardware/driver-specific dependency validation. A systemd unit split alone does not prove per-radio or per-port isolation.
service_orchestration_policy.reboot_boundary: Only explicitly classified changes that genuinely require kernel/firmware restart request systemd reboot; no blanket reboot suppression and no silent AI-board restart.
service_orchestration_policy.shutdown: ASUS hardware/network cleanup must complete before durable data filesystem and vendor runtime files are unmounted.

acceptance_gates: Immutable offline rootfs: dpkg owns every installed file; apt update/install/remove/configure simulation and real isolated install tests; no host-arch ELF, unresolved loader or architecture collisions.
All dynamic executable/plugin closure checks using actual per-ABI loaders and LD_BIND_NOW where appropriate, with and without ld.so.cache; GLIBC_PRIVATE references explicitly accounted for.
Three ABI tests: loader normal execution, pthread/TLS, DNS/NSS, libm, C++ exceptions where used, crypto/CRC CPU execution, time64 and legacy vendor time32 interface checks.
Exact official Ubuntu systemd binary in disposable QEMU on Image-v9 or successor: PID1 boot, unit start/stop/restart/reexec, journald, cgroup ownership, device/sandbox semantics and orderly unmount.
ASUS manager/broker regression with actual libshared notification API, malformed/unauthorized clients, single daemon ownership, missing broker/shim handling and non-ASUS signals unchanged.

Only after kernel/userspace tests, an inactive-slot physical trial: all radios/client association, Ethernet/Runner counters, wired AiMesh, local web edits without global reboot, AI-board bridge/RGB/USB and fallback rollback. A chroot alone cannot validate ASUS hardware startup.
not_done: No ASUS userspace package built or installed by this audit.
No live rootfs replaced or writable partition created.
No claim that all ASUS services work under Ubuntu/systemd259.
No old BE98 binary is asserted to be drop-in safe on BE19000AI.
